summary.goal: Extend the schema with plan-level 'understanding' (agent observations) and step-level 'specification' (architecture/design/testing/security details) to support the Intake -> Planner -> Orchestrator pipeline
summary.context: Current schema only has summary + steps. We need richer structure to capture ideation insights and formal specs. HYBRID MODEL: Understanding is plan-level (context for the whole plan), Specification is step-level (each step has its own arch/design/test/security spec).

model.understanding: Plan-level - what agents observed during ideation (observations, keywords, questions, concerns per role)
model.specification: Step-level - each step can have its own architecture decisions, design elements, test cases, security requirements

in_scope: Zod schemas for Understanding (plan-level) and Specification (step-level)
API endpoints for reading/updating understanding and step specifications
Understanding tab in PlanEditorPage showing agent observations
Tabbed specification editor in StepEditor (Details | Architecture | Design | Testing | Security)
out_of_scope: Automatic agent population of understanding (manual for now)

acceptance_criteria.description: PlanVersion schema includes optional 'understanding' field (record of role -> AgentObservations)
Step schema includes optional 'specification' field with architecture, design, testing, security sub-schemas
Database stores understanding at plan_versions level, specification in steps JSONB
GET /plans/:id/versions/:version returns understanding and steps with specification
PlanEditorPage has Understanding tab (Plan | Understanding | Decisions)
StepEditor shows tabbed spec editor when expanded (Details | Architecture | Design | Testing | Security)
Understanding tab displays observations, keywords, questions, concerns per role
Step spec tabs allow inline editing of each domain's structured fields
Existing plans without understanding/specification continue to work (backward compatible)
MCP tools can read and write understanding and step specifications
